question: According to Census 2011, what proportion of India’s population resided in urban areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**31 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011**, **31% of India’s population** resided in **urban areas**. This percentage highlights the level of urbanization in India during the census year.
 
• The total population of India as per **Census 2011** was approximately **1.21 billion**, out of which **377 million** people lived in urban areas. This accounts for 31% of the total population.
 
• Urbanization is defined as the process by which an increasing proportion of a country’s population resides in urban areas due to factors like migration, industrialization, and urban expansion.
 
• The **31% urban population** is indicative of India’s gradual shift from being a predominantly rural society to one that is increasingly urbanized. However, the majority of the population (69%) still resided in rural areas during this census.
 
• This urbanization trend reflects economic and social changes, including better job opportunities in cities, improved living standards, and migration from rural to urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urbanization in India:**

 
 
• **Urban areas** in India are defined by criteria such as a minimum population of 5,000, a population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometer, and at least 75% of the male working population engaged in non-agricultural activities.
 
• Urbanization in India is primarily driven by factors like **industrial development, infrastructure growth, and rural-to-urban migration**.
 
 
 
• **Breakdown of Census 2011 Data:**
 
 
• The **total rural population** of India was approximately **833 million**, constituting 69% of the total population.
 
• The **urban population** was **377 million**, contributing 31% to the total population.
 
• The **urban growth rate** during the decade from 2001 to 2011 was higher than the rural growth rate, indicating the rapid pace of urbanization.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Urbanization:**
 
 
• Urbanization plays a critical role in economic development as it creates opportunities for industrial growth, employment, and better infrastructure.
 
• However, it also brings challenges like **urban poverty, slums, pollution, and inadequate housing and infrastructure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Comparison:**

 
 
• As of 2011, India’s urbanization level (31%) was **lower than the global average**, which was approximately **52%**.
 
• Countries like the **United States** and **Japan** had urbanization levels exceeding **80%**, highlighting the scope for further urban growth in India.
 
 
 
• **Future Trends:**
 
 
• It is estimated that by **2030**, **40% of India’s population** will reside in urban areas, emphasizing the need for planned urbanization and sustainable development.
 
• Government initiatives like **Smart Cities Mission** and **AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)** are focused on addressing urban challenges and promoting sustainable urban development.
